evals.prompt: Our Next.js app reads process.env all over the place and last week prod started without STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET and silently accepted unsigned webhooks. Set up proper config handling.
evals.expected_output: Creates a single typed env module (e.g., t3-env with Zod) that is the only reader of process.env, separates server and client (NEXT_PUBLIC_) variables, marks secrets as required with no defaults, parses booleans explicitly, validates at build and startup and fails listing invalid keys without values, adds .env.example and a CI key-sync check, replaces scattered process.env reads, and logs a config fingerprint without secret values.
expectations: Creates one config module that is the only place reading process.env and replaces direct reads elsewhere
STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET (and other secrets) are required with no default value
Validation runs at startup and/or build time and fails fast with the list of missing or invalid keys, without printing secret values
Keeps server secrets out of NEXT_PUBLIC_ variables and separates client from server schema
Adds or updates .env.example with placeholder values and keeps .env git-ignored
Does not use z.coerce.boolean() or Boolean(str) for boolean env vars

evals.prompt: I accidentally pushed our production AWS access key and a SendGrid API key to a feature branch on GitHub about an hour ago. I already deleted the file in a new commit. What now?
evals.expected_output: Treats both keys as compromised: rotate/revoke immediately (before history cleanup), check CloudTrail and SendGrid activity for the exposure window, purge from history/logs as policy requires while noting rotation is the actual fix, record the incident, add pre-commit plus CI secret scanning and push protection, and replace the long-lived AWS key with OIDC/workload identity.
expectations: States that deleting the file in a new commit does not remove the secret from history and the keys must be treated as compromised
Revokes or rotates both keys first, before any history rewrite
Checks provider access logs (e.g., CloudTrail, SendGrid activity) for use during the exposure window
Recommends layered secret scanning (pre-commit hook, CI, and platform push protection)
Recommends replacing the long-lived AWS access key with workload identity or OIDC federation

evals.prompt: We want per-PR preview environments. Easiest is to snapshot the production Postgres into each preview so reviewers see real data. Can you set that up on Vercel + Neon?
evals.expected_output: Sets up per-PR previews with a database branch per preview, but refuses raw production copies because they contain PII; proposes anonymized branching (static masking) or a seeded/anonymized parent, runs migrations per preview, uses preview-scoped secrets and sandbox integrations, protects access and adds noindex, handles OAuth/webhooks without widening the prod OAuth app, and adds TTL/teardown on PR close.
expectations: Does not copy raw production data containing PII into previews; proposes anonymized or seeded branches instead
Creates an isolated database branch per preview and runs migrations on it
Uses preview-scoped, low-value secrets and sandbox integrations rather than production secrets
Adds teardown/TTL for previews when the PR closes
Addresses access protection for preview URLs

evals.prompt: Write a GitHub Actions workflow that builds our Docker image, pushes it to ECR, and deploys to ECS with a canary.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this as a pipeline/deployment task owned by deployment-and-infrastructure: routes there (or applies it), with only the config-related parts from this skill — OIDC instead of stored AWS keys and per-environment roles — rather than treating it as an environment-config task.
expectations: Identifies deployment-and-infrastructure as the primary skill for the workflow, build, and canary deploy
Uses OIDC federation with an environment-scoped role instead of storing AWS access keys as secrets
Does not spend the answer on .env files, local dev setup, or config schema design
